summary: Frontend-only retest of the header menu highlight fix. PASS. On all 9 public pages at 1440px, the header nav links (Who We Are, Our Work, Field Notes, Connect, and the Our Work submenu toggle) all show color rgb(96,96,96), weight 400, a transparent background, no background image, no text-decoration, a 0px/transparent bottom border and no box-shadow. This holds for the active link (aria-current=page is set correctly on each page), on hover, on focus, and after clicking (clicking Who We Are, Field Notes or Connect navigates, and the now-active link stays normal). Our Work button stays normal after a click. At 390px the mobile menu opens on 5 pages, all links are normal including the active one, the submenu expands, and clicking Connect navigates. Dropdown items (desktop hover and mobile) are rgb(68,68,68), weight 400, not red, with no hover highlight; the desktop dropdown has its existing white background. Regression: brand-name 32px, brand-sub 11px and links 12px on every page. Live-editor header_styles override (color #1a5e20 / activeColor #0000ff, set in the DB) still wins: non-active links turn green, and the active and hovered links turn blue. The content was then restored with backup_restore_content.py and the diff is clean.

issues: Low priority: the submenu items are rgb(68,68,68) and letter-spaced, while the top links are rgb(96,96,96). They are not red and not highlighted, so this only matters if the client wants a matching grey.

critical_code_review_comments: The fix rule in boxed-layout.css uses :is(*, :hover, :focus, :active, [aria-current=page]) at 4 IDs, and the HeaderStyleTag overrides at 5 IDs still win. That is correct. Note that the editor 'activeColor' field will still deliberately recolour the active and hovered links if an admin sets it.
seed_data_creation: Temporarily set settings.site.header_styles in the DB. Restored afterwards and the diff is clean.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Nav link selector: '#site-header .nav-list .nav-link'. Our Work submenu toggle: button[aria-label$='submenu']. Dropdown items: '#site-header .dropdown a'. The quickest way to test the editor override is to set settings{key:'site'}.header_styles directly after running backup_restore_content.py backup, then restore.
